---
title: "Making My Website Easier to Read"
---

## Why styling matters

For my website, I use a white background, burgundy headings, and a sans-serif font. I want visitors to find the important information quickly and read it comfortably.

## CSS and SCSS

CSS controls the appearance of HTML elements. SCSS adds features such as variables and nesting, then compiles into CSS. In Quarto, a custom SCSS file can extend a Bootstrap theme.

## My theme settings

The project configuration connects the built-in theme and my custom file:

```yaml
format:
  html:
    theme: [cosmo, styles.scss]
```

The variables section sets reusable choices before Bootstrap is compiled:

```scss
/*-- scss:defaults --*/
$primary: #702338;
$body-bg: #ffffff;
$body-color: #252525;
$font-family-sans-serif: Arial, sans-serif;
$font-size-base: 1.125rem;
```

## Styling a specific element

The rules section adds CSS selectors. This example gives a highlighted paragraph a colored border and more space:

```scss
/*-- scss:rules --*/
.portfolio-note {
  border-left: 5px solid $primary;
  padding: 1rem;
  background: #faf3f5;
}
```

::: {.portfolio-note}
**A visible example:** This paragraph uses the custom `portfolio-note` class from my SCSS file.
:::

## Where HTML fits

Quarto converts Markdown into HTML. I can add a small HTML element when I need more control, while keeping most writing in Markdown.

```html
<p class="portfolio-note">A short project takeaway.</p>
```

## My takeaway

Separating content from styling makes the website easier to update. I can change a color or font in one file and apply it across the site. I also need to check contrast, spacing, and navigation on smaller screens.
